title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: The 10-year Treasury yield surged to 5.304%, its highest since May 2002 (surpassing the 2007 peak), after Q2 GDP was revised up to 2.2% and the Fed's preferred inflation gauge (PCE) held at 3.4% y/y in August.

Markets: Stocks were mixed Wednesday — Dow -0.9%, Nasdaq +0.2% as Micron's strong outlook offset margin-narrowing warnings; oil rose ~1.2% to $90.48/bbl as Mideast exports tighten and gold edged up to ~$4,188.
Markets: Asia-Pacific markets opened October rattled — Australia's ASX 200 slid to a four-month low, erasing roughly $50B in value, as financial and industrial stocks dragged amid rising yields.

Macro/Policy: Traders trimmed bets on an October Fed rate hike to ~39% probability after a Fed official signaled no urgency to tighten further, even as growth and inflation data came in firmer than expected.
Macro/Policy: US-Iran negotiations showed little progress, keeping energy-driven inflation concerns elevated; new pharma tariffs are also adding cost pressure in the drug supply chain.

Companies: Accenture reports before today's open (est. EPS $3.19/rev $18.05B) and Nike after the close (est. EPS $0.44/rev $11.35B) — both seen as bellwethers for enterprise AI demand and consumer retail; manufacturing PMI, jobless claims and construction spending data are also due.
